subject: AWS PO: auto-renew flagging + buyer-approval routing
messages:

Subject: Question on auto-renew and approval gating for AWS PO (Everstad)

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. Procurement circulated the PO draft attached and asked two quick clarifications before we proceed to signature:

1) The draft includes a 1-year term with an auto-renew checkbox. Our CFO is sensitive to auto-renew clauses — can you confirm whether the AWS private offer activation requires any Marketplace-side auto-renew flag to be set, or is that purely reflected in the contract we sign?

2) Related: who must approve activation on the buyer side once we accept the private offer? We have a cross-org approval requirement (procurement + engineering security + finance). If Marketplace requires a single approver or a specific hub role, please tell us how that maps to our internal process.

Attached: everstad_po_draft.pdf

If you can point to the exact Marketplace steps (or a doc) that would be great — we want to avoid accidentally enabling an auto-charge on our billing system.

Thanks,
Alice Cho
Senior Procurement Manager
Everstad Technologies

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Cho <alice.cho@everstad.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-19T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on auto-renew and approval gating for AWS PO (Everstad)

Hi Alice — thanks for sending the draft. Quick answers up front, then steps below:

- Auto-renew: AWS Marketplace private offers do not force an "auto-renew" billing action from Marketplace itself. Renewal behavior is determined by the contract/PO and activation parameters in the Seller Private Offer (the Contract Duration field). However, some buyer tooling (especially on the finance side) will create recurring charges if the PO is drafted as recurring. So the safe approach is to mark the PO as non-auto-renew on your contract side and add explicit renewal language for later.

- Buyer approvals: Activation of a private offer typically requires (1) buyer accepts the offer in Marketplace, and (2) buyer finance/procurement issues the Marketplace purchase. AWS enforces that the IAM user who accepts must have the right marketplace/purchase permissions — there isn't a Marketplace-level multi-approver gate. That said, many enterprises use a hub-and-spoke process where procurement accepts and finance runs the wiring.

What we recommend (and what we'd like to coordinate with you):

1) On our side we will set the Private Offer "ActivationRequiresSellerApproval" flag to false so the acceptance flow is initiated by the buyer.
2) We will add a comment in the private offer metadata that the PO is "non-auto-renew, 12-month term, renewal subject to mutual written consent."
3) We can instruct AWS Marketplace support to route any acceptance emails to procurement@everstad.com instead of an individual account owner.

Next steps I propose:
- Neha (cc'd) will confirm the flag change and the metadata addition.
- Vanessa (cc'd) will scope any legal/ops steps on our contract side.

I'll also include an activation runbook snippet you can attach to your internal ticket.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

(attachment: activation-runbook.docx)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Everstad PO - flagging and finance workflow

Team — quick coordination on Everstad (EVR-2028-004):

Summary:
- Buyer (Everstad) wants explicit non-auto-renew language in the PO.
- They also asked how Marketplace acceptance maps to their internal approvers (procurement + security + finance).

Items for our side:
1) Mateo: confirm you told them we'll set ActivationRequiresSellerApproval=false — good. Please mark in the private offer notes that acceptance notifications should go to procurement@everstad.com.
2) Neha: can you confirm whether setting the metadata note is sufficient from an SRE/ops audit perspective, or do we need to create an evidence artifact in our enablement bucket? If evidence is required, how long to produce?
3) Jordan: finance asks whether the offer activation can be staged (accept but not activate billing until finance issues the invoice). My understanding: AWS marks the purchase as active at acceptance; billing start is tied to the contract start date but delaying billing requires seller-side provisioning controls. Can you confirm a safe approach (we don't want to bill before their internal sign-off)?

Proposed mitigations for buyer comfort:
- Add explicit clause to the contract: "Billing to Commence Upon Written Acknowledgement of Finance."
- We can hold activation in our enablement pipeline for up to 72 hours to allow buyer finance to finalize PO release; during that hold we won't provision dedicated resources.

If you confirm the 72-hour hold is operationally okay, we'll offer that as an option to Everstad.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Cho <alice.cho@everstad.com>, procurement@everstad.com
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question on auto-renew and approval gating for AWS PO (Everstad)

Alice — looping back with confirmation and a recommended path forward:

- Auto-renew: We'll annotate the private offer as non-auto-renew and include the contract clause you suggested. That ensures Marketplace won't trigger unexpected charges and gives your finance team control.

- Acceptance routing: We'll set the acceptance notification to procurement@everstad.com. Please ensure the IAM user who will accept has AWS Marketplace purchase permissions (procurement can coordinate with their AWS admin).

- Billing hold option: We can offer a standard 72-hour operational hold between acceptance and provisioning/billing. During that window Redwood will not provision reserved capacity or bill for usage; after 72 hours we will proceed unless we receive written notice from Everstad to extend the hold. If you want us to implement the hold for this PO, reply with a single line: "Please hold activation for 72 hours after acceptance."

Attachments: activation-runbook.docx, everstad_po_draft.pdf

Questions? We're happy to hop on a 15-minute call to walk your finance/admin team through the acceptance steps.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
